title: Enterprise Onboarding: Support, Escalation, Integration & QBR Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates our standard operating procedures for enterprise customer onboarding at Redwood Inference, with a focus on three tightly coupled areas: support handoff and operations, technical escalation, and integration enablement. It also defines how we prepare and run Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and health checks to drive retention and expansion. The document is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call incident responders.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-value for enterprise customers during the first 90 days.
- Ensure predictable, well-documented escalation paths for severity incidents.
- Provide repeatable integration checklists that minimize integration rework.
- Deliver measurable QBRs and health checks that highlight risk and expansion opportunities.

Quick links:
- Onboarding templates: /templates/enterprise-onboarding (internal)
- Escalation matrix: /runbooks/support-escalation-matrix
- Integration checklist (API & VPC): /how-tos/integration-checklist
- QBR slide template: /sales-enablement/qbr-template

1) Roles and ownership:

- Customer Success Manager (CSM): Primary customer contact for business outcomes, adoption tracking, renewal planning, and QBR facilitation.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): Technical lead for integration, architecture reviews, performance tuning, and runbook handoff.
- Support Engineer (L2): Handles triage for production incidents, communicating status to the CSM and SE.
- Escalation On-Call (EOC): Engineering on-call assigned to support severe incidents (S0/S1). Responsible for root cause coordination and postmortem ownership.
- Account Executive (AE): Sales partner for contract or expansion opportunities surfaced during onboarding.

Responsibility table (summary):
- Onboarding plan: CSM (owner), SE (technical owner)
- Integration validation: SE (owner), Support L2 (validation)
- Production runbooks: SE (author), Eng-SRE (review)
- Severity escalation: Support L2 (first responder), EOC (eng escalation)

2) Enterprise onboarding timeline (90-day recommended cadence):

Week 0 (Kickoff):
1. Executive kickoff call (CSM + AE + customer execs) — confirm success criteria and timelines.
2. Technical kickoff (SE + customer infra) — network, auth, and compliance pre-checks.

Week 1–2 (Integration & Access):
- Provide API keys and scoped service accounts.
- Validate network connectivity (VPC peering / PrivateLink / firewall rules). See Integration Checklist below.
- Run first smoke tests: authentication, basic generation, and embeddings.

Week 3–4 (Performance Tuning):
- Collect baseline metrics (latency p50/p95, token cost, QPS).
- Apply batching and caching recommendations (Redwood Optimize suggestions).
- Confirm SLO targets and alert thresholds.

Week 5–8 (Feature Rollout & Validation):
- Enable production routes behind feature flags.
- Verify model rollouts and fallback behavior.
- Execute prompt/eval regression set.

Week 9–12 (Handover & QBR Prep):
- Handover operational runbooks to customer ops and internal SRE.
- Schedule health check and first QBR.
- Capture expansion opportunities and success stories.

3) Integration Checklist (API, Networking, Security):

Minimum required items to mark integration "validated":
- API access: Customer has API key(s) with least privilege scopes.
- Auth verification: Tokens verified against KMS; token rotation process documented.
- Network: VPC peering / PrivateLink or IP allowlist validated; TLS mutual auth tested (if requested).
- Dataflow: Logs and audit-logging destination configured; PII/data residency requirements documented.
- Model catalog: Desired model(s) pinned and performance profile accepted.
- Rate limits: Quotas and burst policies configured in the account controls.
- Observability: Per-route metrics streaming to customer dashboard or shared Grafana.

Checklist table (text):
- Step 1: Provide API key and example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -d '{"input":"hello"}'
- Step 2: Confirm TLS and IP allowlist: Customer to confirm IPs 192.0.2.0/24 (example) are allowed.
- Step 3: Configure logging: Deliver log-forwarding endpoint and verify events for request_id.
- Step 4: Smoke test results: Attach sample output and metrics to onboarding ticket.

4) Support process and SLAs:

Support channels:
- Primary: Support portal (support.redwood.ai) — ticket creation and status.
- Secondary: Dedicated Slack channel (enterprise accounts) — for low-latency communication.
- Emergency: PagerDuty escalation for Sev0/Sev1 incidents.

Severity definitions and target response times (customer-facing SLA):
- Sev0 (Production down, critical business impact): Acknowledgement within 15 minutes; engineering engagement in 30 minutes.
- Sev1 (Major degradation): Acknowledgement within 1 hour; workaround or mitigation plan in 4 hours.
- Sev2 (Partial loss of functionality): Acknowledgement within 4 business hours; corrective action in 3 business days.
- Sev3 (Questions / enhancement requests): Acknowledgement within 1 business day.

Escalation flow (numbered steps):
1. Customer files ticket via portal or Slack. Support L1 triages and attempts remediation.
2. If unresolved within SLA or meets escalation criteria, escalate to Support L2 and notify CSM.
3. Support L2 evaluates, runs diagnostics, and engages EOC if the incident is Sev0/Sev1 or requires code/infra changes.
4. EOC coordinates with Eng-SRE and owning engineering team; regular status updates every 30–60 minutes for Sev0.
5. After resolution, Support leads a blameless postmortem and assigns action items.

Escalation criteria (examples):
- Repeated authentication failures across multiple customers.
- Model-serving latency exceeds p99 SLO by 3x for >15 minutes.
- Data exfiltration suspicion or audit logging missing.

5) Known issues and workarounds (living list):

- Issue: Intermittent 503s when KV cache warms on large context windows.
  Workaround: Temporarily increase concurrency on the route to warm caches, or use a smaller context window until cache warmed. SE to schedule a permanent fix via kernel scheduling patch.

- Issue: Tokenization mismatch between customer tokenizer and model leading to hallucinated truncation.
  Workaround: Provide canonical tokenizer mapping and prompt engineering guidance; recommend model variant with identical tokenizer.

- Issue: VPC peering drop during large data transfers.
  Workaround: Use chunked uploads and enable TCP keepalive; request increased baseline throughput from network team.

For any new workarounds, add an entry to the shared Known Issues board and notify CSM and SE. Classify issues as Security/Performance/Integration/Operational.

6) Health checks & QBR playbook:

Health check cadence and owners:
- Week 2: SE-led technical health check (integration validation).
- Week 6: CSM-led adoption review (usage, high-level metrics).
- Quarterly: Full health check aligned with QBR.

Health check template (bulleted checklist):
- Adoption metrics: active users, API calls per day, peak QPS, tokens/month, embedding volumes.
- Reliability: error rate (5xx), p50/p95 latency, incident count since last check.
- Cost: tokens per conversion, recommended batching/quantization changes.
- Security & Compliance: audit logs present, retention OK, access IAM review done.
- Open actions: list and owner for each item from previous check.

QBR agenda (60–90 minutes):
1. Introductions, participant roles and objectives (5 min).
2. Business outcomes review and adoption highlights (10–15 min).
3. Technical health summary (SE) — metrics and incidents (10–15 min).
4. Cost optimization opportunities (Redwood Optimize suggestions) (10 min).
5. Roadmap alignment & upcoming releases (Product/SE) (10 min).
6. Risks and mitigation plan (CSM) (10 min).
7. Action items and next steps (10 min).

QBR deliverables to share after meeting:
- Slide deck exported from qbr-template with annotated metrics.
- Updated action tracker with owners and due dates.
- Proposed roadmap items or pilot programs (if applicable).

7) Runbooks, templates, and artifacts to attach:

- Onboarding plan template (CSV checklist) — attach to ticket.
- Integration smoke test results (JSON samples and curl commands).
- Production runbook for the account (network diagrams, escalation contacts).
- Postmortem template (blameless) and sample postmortem.

8) Measurement and success criteria:

Primary KPIs (first 90 days):
- Time to first successful production request < 14 days.
- Average onboarding satisfaction score >= 4.2/5.
- Number of Sev1/Sev0 incidents during onboarding <= 1.
- QBR attendance by customer ops/engineering >= 80%.

How we track:
- Onboarding progress tracked in CRM (deal stage) and shared onboarding ticket in Support portal.
- Usage metrics streamed to account dashboard; CSM reviews weekly.

9) Playbook maintenance and review cadence:

- Document owner: Aisha Patel (Customer Success). Responsible for annual review and updates.
- Review cadence: Quarterly sync with SE and Eng-SRE; ad-hoc updates after any Sev0 postmortem where procedural gaps are identified.
- Change log: Maintain a short change log at the top of the account runbook and in this document's Confluence metadata.

10) Appendix: Common CLI snippets and examples:

- Generate example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-v2","input":"Summarize the following..."}'
- Health check query (PromQL example): sum(rate(redwood_request_errors_total[5m])) by (route) / sum(rate(redwood_requests_total[5m])) by (route)
- Escalation contact template (copy into ticket):
  - CSM: name, email, slack
  - SE: name, pager
  - EOC: rotation name, pager

If you have feedback on this playbook or want this adapted to a specific enterprise (HIPAA, SOC2 Type II, or custom on-prem package), contact the owner or add a comment to this page and tag @Aisha Patel.

End of document.
